verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Kanpur leather-goods makers with confirmed export orders and clean receivables; avoid undifferentiated small tanneries and job-work units.
title: Kanpur leather goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
Kanpur leather goods is a conversion business: raw and finished leather in, cut-stitch-assemble out, sold as bags, belts, gloves and footwear. **Cash is made on the cutting table and lost on the receivables ledger.** Value sits in design, buyer approval and finished-goods inventory; the tanning end is commodity and price-taking. The fair at Motijheel shows the demand is real and buyers include foreigners [1], and one stall is selling GPS laptop bags at Rs 4,800 and purses at Rs 2,900 [3] — so when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower sells own-design product at those price points or plain job-work; if plain job-work, ask for the buyer-wise margin sheet.

## What has changed now
Two things moved in Kanpur's favour this month. **The India-New Zealand FTA, effective 20 October 2026, removes up to 10% import duty on 181 products, opening a new market for Kanpur exporters** [2]. Separately, UP GST collections are running +14.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. Against that, India-wide exports are -3.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D] and bank credit is growing +11.9% YoY against output of +2.4% [D] — money is chasing borrowers faster than goods are moving. Peer results are mixed: the listed leather sector shows quarterly sales +13.68% but quarterly profit -4.79% and net margin 6.65% [4], while Sreeleathers posted sales +17.95% and net profit +82.80% in the March 2026 quarter [7]. **Treat the FTA as an order-flow opportunity, not yet as proven cash.**

## Where to grow
Pursue the export-ready converter: units with own designs, a named overseas buyer and a demonstrated ability to meet quality standards, since the FTA benefit reaches small and mid units too [2]. **Prioritise borrowers who can show a New Zealand buyer enquiry or order in hand, and who already sell own-label product.** Avoid pure job-work units, single-buyer dependents and tanneries with no finished-goods line.

## How to grow safely
Structure against the order, not the balance sheet. **Take the export order copy, buyer-wise sales register and stock statement every month**, plus GST returns and bank statements. Keep tenor matched to the receivables cycle; ask for the actual credit period from customer. Where forex exposure exists, insist on a hedging policy — Super Tannery recorded a Rs 0.45 crore forex loss in FY24 without one [11].

## Early-warning signs
- Monthly stock statement versus sales: inventory rising while sales flat -> stop fresh limits and inspect godown. - Buyer concentration: top buyer above half of sales -> ask for the second-buyer pipeline before renewal. - Receivable days stretching beyond the stated credit period -> move to order-backed limits only. - Forex loss line appearing in quarterly accounts -> require hedging before enhancing.
watch: Inventory up with flat sales -> freeze limit enhancement and inspect stock
Filing gaps or falling turnover -> re-rate the account and seek fresh buyer proof
Cheque returns or overdraft usage -> convert to order-backed limit
No shipment against FTA order in two months -> treat FTA benefit as unproven
Unhedged loss recorded -> mandate hedging before renewal
